MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  FEBRUARY 14, 2017

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 7:00 p.m. in the City Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by
MAYOR ZERUNYAN.

ROLL CALL
City Council Members Present: Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Staff Present:  City Manager Doug Prichard
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Planning Director David Wahba

Others Present:  Lou Persichina, Park and Activities Commission

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The PVP 4-H Club led the audience in the Pledge of Allegiance.

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

  NONE

5.  ROUTINE MATTERS

A.  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JANUARY 18, 2017

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE THE ADJOURNED  CITY  COUNCIL  MINUTES  OF
  JANUARY 18, 2017 AS PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

B.  ADJOURNED JOINT CITY COUNCIL AND PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES
  OF JANUARY 24, 2017

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE THE ADJOURNED JOINT CITY COUNCIL AND PLANNING
  COMMISSION MINUTES OF JANUARY 24, 2017 AS PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

C.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JANUARY 24, 2017

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO APPROVE THE CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JANUARY 24, 2017 AS
  PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
FEBRUARY 14, 2017
 D.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – JANUARY AND FEBRUARY

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO APPROVE WARRANTS 57962 THROUGH 58002 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $150,420.10; SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 010117 THROUGH 010217;
  57833 THROUGH 57837; 57857 (VOID); 57862 (VOID); 57867
  THROUGH 57891; 57930 THROUGH 57952 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $266,688.79 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $417,108.89 WITH
  PROPER AUDIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR: The following routine matters will be acted upon by one
  vote to approve with the majority consent of the City Council. There will be no
  separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior
  to the roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to
  the City Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be
  read by title only.

  APPROVED.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

7.  AUDIENCE ITEMS  NOT  ON  THE  AGENDA/WRITTEN  AND  ORAL
  COMMUNICATIONS

A.  AJ Poulin requested that the COUNCIL allocate funding for trail improvements
  in the Dapplegray neighborhood.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN noted that several projects have been assigned funding
  including June’s Trail. He further noted that storm drains on Buckskin Lane
  are also being reviewed.

  Planning Director Wahba provided an update on how the City is moving forward
  with June’s Trail and that engineering design and cost estimates are being
  prepared. Additionally, he stated that staff and MAYOR ZERUNYAN are
  attempting to set up a workshop with interested residents.

  Laura Walters, Los Angeles County Fire Department, reported that the
  January 22 rains caused the second busiest day for 911 calls in the
  Department’s history. She noted that all fire stations provide sand bags and
  emergency preparation information is available at fire.lacounty.gov.

  Ms. Walters mentioned the dangers of storm channels and advised against
  driving through flooded areas.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN thanked the Fire Department for their assistance and
  commented that the City also offers pre-filled sand bags at the Howlett Park
  Maintenance Yard.

  City Manager Prichard noted that being prepared is of the utmost importance
  and advised residents to take precautions ahead of time to minimize flooding.

  Community Services Director Clark announced that the Howlett Park
  Equestrian Center will provide emergency shelter for horses in the event the
  upcoming rains cause any problems in backyard barns.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
FEBRUARY 14, 2017
 8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS/MEETINGS

  NONE

9.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 6, 2017

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  FEBRUARY 6, 2017.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

10.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  SALARY ADMINISTRATION POLICY

  Recommendation:  That the City Council adopt the salary administration
  policies.

  City Manager Prichard provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ, City Manager Prichard noted that the
  Consumer Price Index (CPI) would be considered on an April to April basis and
  explained that this period would be the most relevant while still allowing for
  preparation of the budget.

  Brief discussion ensued regarding the frequency of surveys and the factors that
  any cost of living adjustments would take into consideration.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF noted her recollection that a salary survey had not been
  completed in ten years and although it may need to be updated, she was
  concerned about the long term impacts of unchecked increases to salaries.

  City Manager Prichard explained the process by which initial salaries are
  established when making a hiring decision and then upon performance review.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF commented that she would like more time to consider
  this due to the fact that pensions are out of control.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted that PERS pensions are owed to employees
  and that the City has little control over the cost to meet this obligation.

  City Manager Prichard commented that the COUNCIL should be proud of the way
  salaries have been handled in good times and bad and that the staff has always
  been valued.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN concurred with City Manager Prichard’s comments noting
  that it is only fair in good times to reward the staff when they stood by the City
  through the difficult times. He reiterated that this policy is a guideline to assist in
  the deliberation process.

  City Manager Prichard commented that the goals in the policy are guiding
  principles and makes for good salary administration as recommended by the
  consultant.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN

  TO ADOPT THE SALARY ADMINISTRATION POLICIES AND BRING BACK
  A PROPOSAL TO CONDUCT THE SALARY SURVEY.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
FEBRUARY 14, 2017
 B.  HOWLETT PARK EQUESTRIAN CENTER STRUCTURES BID RESULTS

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the purchase and delivery of
  the horse show and dressage show booths only, including the installation of
  concrete foundations and utility connections, for an estimated cost of $71,400
  funded by Los Angeles County Excess Proposition A Funds.

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL, Community Services Director Clark
  noted that this particular firm has previously performed this type of work. She
  then inquired about the appearance of the building and if there were any
  renderings submitted for review. Community Services Director Clark noted that
  the subcommittee was pleased with the estimate and appearance of the buildings.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted that only the subcommittee reviewed the
  renderings and not the entire Equestrian Committee.

  After further discussion, it was the consensus of the COUNCIL

  TO DIRECT STAFF TO PROVIDE ADDITIONAL INFORMATION ON THE
  FOUNDATION AND RENDERINGS AT THE NEXT MEETING.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

11.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

  NONE

12.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS: This item provides the
  opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information and reports to
  other Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or activities of
  currently active Council Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide
  governmental associations, special districts and/or joint powers authorities and
  their various committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or
  have an interest, which are not otherwise agendized.

A.  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN reported that he attended the Community Choice
  Aggregation (CCA) meeting where discussion included finalizing the Joint
  Powers Authority.

B.  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL reported that she and COUNCILMAN
  ZUCKERMAN attended the SCAG Earthquake Preparedness presentation. She
  noted that discussion included major threats of water supply and fire
  suppression.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN referred to an ordinance for seismic improvements
  required at the time of private property ownership changes and suggested this
  item be included in the Policy Development Session.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN commented that he was impressed with the Sheriff
  Department’s 3D earthquake presentation and suggested that the South Bay
  Cities Council of Governments (SBCCOG) might be interested in having them
  make the same presentation. COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN suggested including
  this presentation at the City’s Annual Emergency Preparedness Expo at the
  Norris Pavilion.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
FEBRUARY 14, 2017
 13.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS: This item provides the opportunity for Members
  of the City Council to request information on currently pending projects and/or
  issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized for future consideration
  and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

A.  MEASURE H – “LOS ANGELES COUNTY PLAN TO PREVENT AND COMBAT
  HOMELESSNESS”

  Recommendation:  That the City Council discuss the issues and provide
  direction to staff.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted that homelessness is a very serious
  situation across the nation and brought this item to the COUNCIL for
  consideration as it will be on the March ballot.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF noted that this measure is a continuation of the
  partnership with Los Angeles County, the SBCCOG and People Assisting the
  Homeless (PATH). She encouraged everyone to think about addressing this
  issue and stated that this measure would add .25% local sales tax and bring in
  approximately $350 million dollars a year for 10 years to provide temporary and
  permanent housing services. Additionally, she noted that the Palos Verdes
  Peninsula Chamber of Commerce has voted to support this measure.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN commented that certain communities have found
  that it costs less money to provide housing than spending law enforcement time
  and effort to address this problem.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN expressed his personal belief not to take a formal
  position on behalf of the COUNCIL and preferred to leave it up to the residents
  to make their own informed decisions.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN commented that homelessness is a very important issue
  that affects everyone. He further noted his disappointment with how state and
  national governments have handled this crisis, and it is his hope that this local
  program will be managed correctly.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO APPROVE BRINGING BACK A  RESOLUTION  SUPPORTING
  MEASURE H AT THE NEXT MEETING.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Zerunyan
  ABSTAIN:  Schmitz
  NOES:  Zuckerman

  ***

  At 8:44 p.m., the City Council convened into Closed Session.

  ***

14.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  DISCUSSION WITH RESPECT TO PUBLIC EMPLOYMENT: QUARTERLY CITY
  MANAGER EVALUATION (Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957)

  NO ACTION WAS TAKEN.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
FEBRUARY 14, 2017
   ***

  At 9:30 p.m., the COUNCIL reconvened into open session with MAYOR
  ZERUNYAN, MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL,
  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ, and COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN present.

  ***

15.  ADJOURNMENT IN MEMORY OF MARTIN J. MAYER, CITY PROSECUTOR

  At 9:30 p.m. MAYOR ZERUNYAN formally adjourned the City Council meeting
  to 5:30 p.m. on February 28, 2017 for the purpose of conducting current
  Equestrian Committee interviews.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Hope J. Nolan  Douglas R. Prichard
Deputy City Clerk  City Clerk

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
FEBRUARY 14, 2017
